To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) replication dependent histone gene transcription occurs in retinal progenitor cells, differentiating neurons and in aging neurons, (2) transcription of replication dependent genes varies across the retina during development, and (3) the transcription of replication dependent gene expression is independent of the rapamycin mediated inhibition of mTOR pathway.
replication dependent histones are actively transcribed throughout retinal development, and that the transcription of these histones is not regulated by the mTOR pathway.
replication dependent histones genes are transcribed in a cell type specific and age dependent manner.

the transcriptional regulation and function of histone genes in neurons
understanding the transcriptional control of replication dependent histon genes in the developing and senescent retina, which is a model for studying neurodegenerative diseases.
the regulation of the expression of histone genes in neurons during development and aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of histone genes is not only limited to the S phase of the cell cycle but also in the differentiating and aging retina.
replication dependent histones are expressed in differentiating neurons, and that their expression is not regulated by mTOR pathway in the aging retina.
the transcription of replication dependent paralogenes occurs in a cell cycle independent manner in differentiating retinal neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcription of replication dependent paralogenes is not only regulated during development, but also in aging neurons.
histone genes, which are traditionally associated with replication, are also transcribed in different retinal neurons during development and aging.
the transcription of replication dependent (and replication independent) histone genes in neurons may have an important functional role in neuronal development and maintenance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of replication dependent genes is not only restricted to the S-phase of the cell cycle but also occurs during differentiation and aging.
replication dependent histones are not only transcribed embryonically, but also in postmitotic cells during retinal development, and in senescent cells during aging.
the expression of replication dependent paralogue histone genes in retinal neurons is not only developmentally regulated, but also occurs in the aging retina.
